title: GPU slab-aware demotion + predictive trim orchestrator for KV cache correctness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As model-serving workloads increase, the KV cache must evict or demote entries in a way that minimizes expensive recompute while keeping GPU memory fragmentation low and correctness guarantees intact. Current LRU/TTL heuristics evict unevenly across GPU slab classes and can evict hot prefixes when continuous batching briefly spikes, causing tail-latency regressions and quality churn.

This ticket proposes a GPU slab-aware demotion plus predictive trim orchestrator: a hybrid policy that demotes cold entries to a compact 'demotion slab' per GPU memory class, uses short probabilistic TTLs to allow transient spikes to recover, and trims the demotion slab with workload-aware predictive trimming derived from recent batch/prefix patterns. The orchestrator must provide correctness invariants (no observable stale-pointer usages, prefix-affinity safety during in-flight batches) and an incremental rollout plan with telemetry and fuzz testing.

Goals: 1) Reduce regressive recompute for bursty prefix access patterns; 2) Improve slab compaction to reduce fragmentation and avoid expensive full-GPU defragmentation; 3) Maintain strong safety invariants for in-flight requests and multi-threaded cache access; 4) Provide observability and canary rollout controls.

Non-goals: Replace global LRU; change model KV layout; Introduce speculative prefetching in this scope (future follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary on dedicated cluster shows <=5% increase in p99 token latency under synthetic burst traffic vs baseline
No production crashes or invalid memory reads in staged canary (sanity, ASAN-like checks in debug builds)
Telemetry exposes demotion slab hit-rate, trim decisions, and per-prefix eviction traces for debugging
Automated fuzz suite detects zero cases of use-after-evict for in-flight batches in CI
design_decisions: Use a per-GPU 'demotion slab' for compacted items rather than immediate free-list reclamation to reduce fragmentation
Demotion triggers: age-based until probabilistic TTL, OR cost-signature threshold (recompute cost estimate) OR explicit controller signals during memory pressure
Predictive trim uses a lightweight sliding-window sketch of recent prefix sees and batch coalescing to proportionally trim low-utility demotion entries
Safety: entries moved to demotion slab retain stable read handles; full eviction only happens after demotion age + no active handles + prefix-stability check
Controller exposes a graceful back-off to avoid trimming when observed batch replays show repeated prefix reactivation
telemetry: metrics.kv.demote.count: counter of items demoted per GPU
metrics.kv.demote.latency_ms: histogram of demotion move latency
metrics.kv.trim.decision_rate: number of trim decisions per minute
metrics.kv.demote.hit_ratio: hit rate observed for demoted slab
traces.kv.eviction_trace: per-request event trace with timestamps for demote/evict/reload
rollout_plan: 1) Implementation behind dynamic flag and config knobs (default off)
2) Unit + integration tests in CI with debug assertions enabled
3) Internal canary on staging cluster with 2 GPUs; run synthetic burst suite for 48 hours
4) Gradual production rollout: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks, with automatic rollback on metric regressions
5) Post-rollout follow-up to consider prefetching and cross-GPU demotion coordination
testing_plan: Deterministic unit tests for demotion and pointer stability
Integration test that replays historical traffic traces to assert no correctness regressions
Fuzz harness that simulates concurrent readers/writers and in-flight batch KV pinning
Memory-safety debug builds on canary hardware with sanitizer checks
Load test with continuous batching patterns (short bursts, long-tail prefixes) to measure p50/p95/p99 token latency
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keeping demoted entries consumes GPU memory but reduces costly recompute; we target a small percentage (configurable) bounded by slab quotas
We considered full generational GC but rejected due to complexity and rollback risk during rollout
Need to align with autoscaler signals so demotion does not mask true capacity pressure
Will coordinate with 'batching heuristics' team to surface prefix coalescing metrics used by predictor
